front: Why does a transformer need positional information?
back: Attention is permutation-equivariant: $Z(PX)=PZ(X)$. Without position signal, word order is invisible.

front: Why sine and cosine in pairs?
back: A shift by $k$ becomes a fixed rotation of each pair, independent of $p$: a linear map the model can learn.
Fast pairs distinguish neighbours, slow pairs encode coarse location (like second, minute and hour hands).
Trainable table $(T_{\max},d)$ added to token embeddings (GPT-2). No rows beyond $T_{\max}$; $T_{\max}d$ parameters.
Rotate each coordinate pair of $q$ and $k$ by an angle $m\theta_i$ proportional to position; the dot product then depends on $m-n$ only.

front: 2-D rotation matrix and its key identities
Does RoPE change vector norms? Add parameters?
back: No to both: rotations preserve norms and the angles are fixed functions of position.
To $Q$ and $K$ (not $V$), per head, inside every attention layer; shape stays $(B,h,T,d_h)$.
No position vectors: add a head-specific penalty $-m_h|i-j|$ to the scores; mentioned in the source lesson as good at length extrapolation.
The mask breaks permutation symmetry a little (a token sees only its prefix) but gives no distance information.
